checks_performed: Read the exact target from the authorized source JSON and audited the complete authorized draft; no other source file or web resource was used.
Reconstructed the radius-one matching-edit normal forms, the separator counting argument, and every positive and negative construction directly from the definitions.

Checked that each claimed algorithm is polynomial: greedy deletion has at most n/3 iterations, local-cut improvement has at most |E| strict improvements, and the dense-side condition reduces to ordinary bipartite matching.

Exhaustively checked all 32,777 labeled graphs of orders 0, 3, and 6 using integer bit masks and exact enumeration of triangle partitions. The checker reported 14,731 positive constructions and 18,046 negative constructions overall, with no counterexample.

Verified the W_a construction symbolically, including its order, absence of a good-triple factor, dissociation number, triangle-support connectivity, resistance to triangle-eliminating matching deletion, and separator certificate.
Compared the complete requested target against the established branches. No argument exhausts all graphs or disproves exact FP membership.

claims.claim: A graph G has a radius-one neighbor with a triangle partition if and only if V(G) has a partition into triples each spanning at least two edges of G; moreover, a positive output may use additions only.
claims.evidence: If Δ(E(G) symmetric-difference E(H))≤1, the changed edges form a matching. Within any H-triangle, two edges absent from G would be two changed edges sharing a vertex, which is impossible; hence the triple spans at least two G-edges. Conversely, for each triple spanning exactly two G-edges, add its unique missing edge. These additions lie in disjoint triples and therefore form a matching, while triples already spanning three edges need no edit. This proves both directions and the additions-only normal form.
claims.search_method: Direct proof reconstruction from the radius-one metric and a complete necessity/converse case split on each partition triple.

claims.claim: Every radius-one negative output can be replaced by one obtained solely by deleting a matching from G.
claims.evidence: Write H=(G-D)+A, where D and A are disjoint subsets of the matching E(G) symmetric-difference E(H). Then H0=G-D=H-A is a subgraph of H. Any triangle partition of H0 would also be a triangle partition of H, contradicting negativity. Thus H0 is negative and differs from G only by deleting the matching D.
claims.search_method: Direct monotonicity proof after separating the symmetric-difference matching into additions and deletions.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially checkable modulo-three separator certificate for negative outputs.
claims.evidence: Let C be a component of T(H)-X. Every partition triangle avoiding X lies wholly within one such component. A partition triangle meeting non-X vertices from two components is impossible because the edge between those vertices belongs to that triangle, hence to T(H), and would join the components. If |C| is nonzero modulo three, at least one triangle covering C must therefore meet X. Distinct such components require distinct partition triangles, and those disjoint triangles consume distinct vertices of X. Consequently q≤|X| for every triangle partition, so q>|X| certifies negativity. Triangles, T(H), its components, their orders, X, and a proposed matching deletion are all polynomially checkable.
claims.search_method: Direct modular counting and injection argument, including all possibilities for how a partition triangle intersects X and T(H)-X.

claims.claim: If S⊆V satisfies |S|>n/3 and Δ(G[S])≤1, then a valid negative output is constructible in polynomial time from S.
claims.evidence: Because Δ(G[S])≤1, E(G[S]) is a matching. Delete precisely those edges to obtain H, making S independent while staying at radius one. Each H-triangle contains at most one vertex of S, so n/3 disjoint triangles could cover at most n/3 vertices of S, strictly fewer than |S|. Thus H has no triangle partition, and the construction is plainly polynomial.
claims.search_method: Direct construction followed by an exact pigeonhole count over the n/3 putative partition triangles.

claims.claim: A greedy polynomial algorithm resolves every input except possibly when it leaves between 1 and n/3 vertices.
claims.evidence: Each selected center and two remaining neighbors gives a disjoint triple spanning at least two original edges. At termination no remaining vertex has two remaining neighbors, so Δ(G[R])≤1. If R is empty, Claim 0 completes all removed triples using matching additions. If |R|>n/3, Claim 3 constructs a negative output. There are at most n/3 greedy iterations, so the procedure is polynomial; only 0<|R|≤n/3 is left untreated.
claims.search_method: Loop-invariant and terminal-case proof, checking disjointness, remainder degree, both output branches, and iteration count.

claims.claim: Given X with |X|<n/3 and Δ(G-X)≤3, a valid negative output can be constructed in polynomial time. Consequently this applies whenever fewer than n/3 vertices of G have degree at least four.
claims.evidence: Starting from any cut of G-X, repeatedly flip a vertex having more same-side than opposite-side neighbors. Each flip strictly increases the integer cut size, so at most |E(G-X)| flips occur. At local maximality, same-side degree is at most half the total residual degree and hence at most one because Δ(G-X)≤3. The monochromatic edges thus form a matching D. Deleting D makes H-X bipartite, so every H-triangle meets X. A partition into n/3 disjoint triangles would require at least n/3 distinct vertices of X, contradicting |X|<n/3. Taking X as the vertices of G-degree at least four gives Δ(G-X)≤3 and proves the consequence.
claims.search_method: Direct potential-function analysis of local cut improvement and a triangle-cover counting contradiction.

claims.claim: There is a polynomially recognizable dense-side condition producing a positive output.
claims.evidence: Under the stated condition, matching two clones of each c∈C to L supplies two distinct, globally disjoint G-neighbors for every c. These form |C| good triples. Every vertex of L has at most one nonneighbor in all of G, so the complement induced by any triple of unused L-vertices has maximum degree at most one and hence at most one edge; each such triple therefore spans at least two G-edges. The unused count is n-3|C|=3(n/3-|C|), so it partitions into triples. Claim 0 then supplies matching additions. Clone saturation is recognizable and constructible by polynomial-time bipartite matching.
claims.search_method: Direct verification of the clone-matching construction, unused-vertex divisibility, and complement-degree case analysis inside an arbitrary leftover triple.

claims.claim: The complete target is solvable for n=0,3,6.
claims.evidence: The greedy remainder has size divisible by three. For n=3 or 6, every nonempty remainder therefore has size at least three, which is greater than n/3, while an empty remainder gives the positive branch; n=0 has the empty positive partition. The persisted exact checker independently enumerated all 1+8+32,768=32,777 labeled graphs. It validated radius-one edits and positive partitions directly and exhaustively enumerated all triangle partitions when validating negative outputs. It reported n=0: 1 positive; n=3: 4 positive and 4 negative; n=6: 14,726 positive and 18,042 negative; no counterexample occurred.
claims.search_method: Exhaustive integer-bit-mask enumeration of every labeled graph of orders 0, 3, and 6, using exact recursive enumeration of all vertex partitions into triples and no floating-point decisions.

claims.claim: For every integer a≥2 there is a connected, triangle-support-connected graph W_a of order 3(5a+2) having no P3/triangle factor although its largest induced subgraph of maximum degree one has only 10<n/3 vertices.
claims.evidence: Five cliques of order 3a+1 plus the universal vertex z have order 5(3a+1)+1=3(5a+2). A good triple avoiding z cannot cross cliques, since such a triple spans at most one edge. The unique factor triple containing z meets at most two cliques, leaving at least three cliques with all 3a+1 vertices; those cannot be internally partitioned into triples. Hence no good-triple factor exists. A dissociation set containing z has size at most two; one avoiding z has at most two vertices per clique, and selecting two from each clique attains 10. Since a≥2, 10<5a+2=n/3. Every clique edge lies in a clique triangle, and every z-to-clique edge lies in a triangle using another vertex of that clique, so T(W_a)=W_a is connected.
claims.search_method: Symbolic case split according to the factor triple containing z, followed by exact modular arithmetic and a complete dissociation-set case split.

claims.claim: The family W_a also shows that restricting the negative branch to making the graph triangle-free by a matching deletion is insufficient, while the separator certificate detects its negative answer.
claims.evidence: Each clique has 3a+1≥7 vertices. The edges deleted inside it by any global matching partition its affected vertices into disjoint pairs; choosing vertices from three distinct pair/singleton blocks yields three mutually undeleted clique edges and hence a surviving triangle. Thus no matching deletion makes W_a triangle-free. With no deletion and X={z}, T(W_a)-X consists of five clique components, each of order 3a+1 nonzero modulo three. Therefore q=5>|X|=1, and Claim 2 certifies that W_a has no triangle partition.
claims.search_method: Direct matching-block argument inside a clique and exact evaluation of the separator certificate for X={z}.

target_evidence: The exact target asks for one polynomial-time procedure handling every graph of order divisible by three, or a rigorous disproof of that exact FP-membership statement. The draft establishes correct normal forms, several polynomial positive and negative branches, complete handling of orders 0, 3, and 6, and an infinite family refuting two narrower proposed dichotomies. These are material advances, but no proof shows that the branches exhaust all input graphs, and W_a refutes only those narrower strategies—not Sidestep membership itself. The final writeup explicitly says the general FP claim remains unresolved and makes no full-membership or hardness claim. Accordingly the target coverage is valid partial progress, and the draft's claimed_resolution of PARTIAL is accurate rather than overstated or understated.
